correctness.rationale: The geometric proof derives the two complement shapes from 3-line concurrency, proves every trace on a four-arc using secants/tangents/external lines, shatters collinear and noncollinear triples, excludes any four-set containing a collinear triple by the all-zero trace, and excludes five-sets using the maximum arc size. All 8192 supports and all 286 hypotheses were independently enumerated in coordinate and cyclic incidence models; outputs matched exact face and facet counts. The finite census corroborates, but does not replace, the combinatorial proof.

originality.rationale: A 2018 halfspace-union paper and a 2025 real-line-union primary text do not imply the exact-three-distinct-line ternary-projective trace classification. A particularly close existing order-three finite projective two-line classification has different concepts and explicitly leaves three or more lines outside its scope. Literal, alias, parameter, and implied-statement queries found no stronger triple-line coverage; prior literature may be unindexed or use different language. Known four-arc counts alone do not state the Boolean shattering characterization or complement-to-facet duality.

value.rationale: Determines the entire shattering complex of a canonical 13-point finite incidence geometry, including nonpure facet types and a bijection with complements of all 286 concepts. It exhibits a structural obstruction: a collinear triple is shattered but cannot be extended by any fourth point, while all noncollinear triples extend to four-arcs. All-degree exact counts and a sharp 702-to-234 reduction in shattered four-sets when comparing exact two versus three distinct-line hypotheses give substantive information beyond VC dimension.
